close_reason: Replaced 'as u64' with u64::try_from + .ok() at memory.rs:401 (now at ~408 after comment expansion). Added inline comment documenting the year-2554 u64 nanos overflow boundary and the cargo-cult-avoidance rationale. cargo clippy --features memory,realistic-demo-ids --tests -- -D warnings clean. cargo test under same features clean.
description: memory.rs:325: `.map(|d| d.as_nanos() as u64).unwrap_or(1_000_000_000)`. `Duration::as_nanos()` returns u128; the `as u64` is a silent high-bit truncation. — In practice the truncation never matters: u64 nanos covers ~584 years from UNIX epoch, so the high u128 bits are guaranteed zero through year ~2554. But `as u64` reads as 'author skipped the conversion check'. Idiomatic Rust is `u64::try_from(d.as_nanos()).unwrap_or(1_000_000_000)` — same fallback, but the truncation case is explicit (and would catch a future hypothetical Duration arithmetic that overflowed u64 nanos). — This is the same call-site that produces the demo-id base nanoseconds; pairing the truncation with the existing CARGO-CULT WARNING comment block (the deterministic path already disclaims production use) would be 30 seconds of work. Engineering impact: cosmetic in this exact place, but the pattern repeats: `as` casts that are correct-by-platform-assumption appear three other places in this crate (the cluster in JMAP-826m.45). Making this one explicit is one less cargo-cult example for downstream copiers.
title: realistic-demo-ids: as_nanos() as u64 silently truncates the u128 source
